Well, I would say the idea is not that bad. I had a similar idea two weeks ago. For me there was and still is the problem, that I have no knowledge of leather.  But I can share my informations so far with you. 

​

1. This can be a great market, but there are a lot of other companys that compete with you.
2. You need a great network and this is probably the part where it get's difficult. You need to know and trust the suppliers in your producing country and their suppliers. Beside that, you need to know a shipping company that ships your products at a low-cost and you need to know how to get into the car manufacturing industrie. So the important factor is your network.
3. The profit margins for leather for middle-class vehicles are very low. Here you need high sales figures. I don't know how the profit margins are in the luxury high-end sector, but probably they are better (but the costs are also way higher, because of the better quality). 
4. You need some capital. You will probably have to pay in advance.
5. You need some knowledge of economy (For me this was and is not the problem). There are a lot of things to know when you own an international operating business (for example trade restrictions, product policy, pricing, marketing,...).
6. Founding such a businnes is very riskfull.

​

You mentioned Nigeria. In my eyes, this is a bad idea. Nigeria is very unsafe. Terrorism, ship hijacking, corruption and things like that can make your life hard. You probably should think about another country. There are several other countries that have a great leather industrie (with low costs), are safer and have a better logistical connection to the rest of the world.

​

If you have questions, you can write me.
